name: Congregation Apparel
old_description: As a team of dedicated designers and artisans, we aim to provide quality screen printing and embroidery, while inspiring communities to come together and create!
about:
Congregation Apparel operates from Pewaukee, Wisconsin, where founders Jordan and Kelsey Shimon run the business as a family-owned venture. The couple, who also serve as youth pastors in Corpus Christi, Texas, started the company out of a shared passion for clothing as a means of building community. While the exact founding year is not publicly disclosed, the brand emphasizes its Midwestern roots and a mission to gather people through custom apparel.

The shop specializes in screen printing and embroidery for custom garments, offering a full design-to-delivery workflow that includes digital mock‑ups for client approval, vector artwork conversion, and an optional online pop‑up storefront with a dedicated URL for selling gear. Production runs start at 24 pieces per design, with samples available for orders of 100 or more. Turnaround typically falls between 14 and 21 business days, though rush requests can be accommodated.

Clients range from schools and sports teams to churches, businesses, and community groups across the United States. The company services southeastern Wisconsin and south Texas in person, while handling national orders remotely by phone and email. Wholesale brand selection is curated by the owners, who leverage deep catalog knowledge to match fabrics and styles to each project.

The Shimon’s frame their work as stewardship—turning raw materials into wearable expressions of identity and unity. They cite quality, creativity, and community as the pillars that differentiate their service, aiming to make the ordering process collaborative rather than transactional.
